key_insight: Brain-Adapter combines report-guided attention and visual MIL to turn pre-trained 2D biomedical VLMs into a scalable 3D CT diagnosis system for acute intracranial pathologies.
clinical_relevance: It could help automate scan-level multi-label brain CT triage without dense voxel-level annotations, supporting faster and more scalable critical-care imaging workflows.
method: Uses raw diagnostic sentences as text queries in a Text-Conditioned Attention (TCA) module to align image regions with disease concepts.
Runs a parallel visual MIL stream supervised by structured labels extracted with an LLM to capture global scan-level signals.
Fuses both streams with a consistency constraint during training and an uncertainty-aware refinement step at inference.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive experiments showing Brain-Adapter outperforms state-of-the-art 3D models and standard MIL baselines on comprehensive 3D CT diagnosis.
watch_item: Performance and robustness may depend on the quality of extracted report labels and the consistency of the source reports across institutions.
paper_title: Brain-Adapter: A Dual-Stream Vision-Language MIL Framework for Comprehensive 3D CT Diagnosis of Acute Intracranial Pathologies
